entities.summary:
Drest X (drest-x) was the Pictish king who ruled from 845 to 848 CE, a pivotal moment in Scottish and British history.

As the son of Uurad, Drest's ascension marked the beginning of a tumultuous era of power struggles between the Picts and Kenneth MacAlpin. The Pictish Chronicle chronicles his reign, which was marked by conflict with his rival, who would eventually unite the Picts and Scots under a single monarchy.

Drest's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, as his son Uurad II succeeded him and continued to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized this period. The historical record suggests that Drest's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against Kenneth MacAlpin, who would eventually emerge victorious.

Despite his eventual downfall, Drest X remains an important figure in the annals of Scottish history, offering valuable insights into the intricate politics and power dynamics of this pivotal era.
